decisions.reason: As a newly launched dental thermoforming consumable with its own product page, it fits the firm's core laboratory workflow offering and is inexpensive to keep on the market while demand uncertainty is still resolving.

This PETG thermoforming blank is closely adjacent to the firm's established materials business, and in the first year the option value of learning about uptake is likely higher than the modest cost of continuing it.

The UV-curing lacquer appears to be a small complementary material whose limited carrying cost justifies keeping it available until the firm learns more about repeat demand and cross-selling potential.
The intraoral contrast spray supports digital and clinical workflows that are central to the firm's strategy, so keeping it preserves an attractive option in a growing digital ecosystem.

A custom earmold line uses the firm's existing custom-manufacturing and hearing-care capabilities, making it sensible to keep this early-stage option open rather than exit before market feedback matures.

Custom hearing protection earmolds are strongly related to the firm's hearing-care customer base, and a large established manufacturer would typically continue such a recent launch while uncertainty remains high and capabilities are already in place.
